# Plainsay

> Plainsay is a free, MIT-licensed dictation app for Mac. In Local mode,
> Whisper or Parakeet transcribes entirely on your Mac — no account or
> subscription. Optional Plainsay Cloud sends recorded audio for hosted
> transcription and Polishing without a transcription-model download for 12
> PLN gross/month (VAT included; about US$3), with 900 transcription minutes per rolling 30 days.

Plainsay is a from-scratch Swift/SwiftUI menu-bar app: global hotkey capture,
a choice of local Core ML transcription (WhisperKit or NVIDIA Parakeet TDT
0.6B v3 via FluidAudio), hosted transcription, an optional Polishing pass that
turns spoken language into written language, and paste-based text insertion.
The client is fully open source; a separate, deliberately opt-in Plainsay
Cloud tier exists for people who don't want to manage a local model or an API
key.

Plainsay and Plainsay Cloud are operated by DMT Sp. z o.o. in Poland.

A single dictation can run for up to 10 minutes. Plainsay stops recording and
processes the captured audio at that boundary.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/conrader/plainsay/blob/main/README.md): install, first launch, architecture, how it works
- [Source](https://github.com/conrader/plainsay): the whole client, MIT licensed
- [Releases](https://github.com/conrader/plainsay/releases): notarized builds, changelog
- [Homepage](https://plainsay.app/): overview, pricing, screenshots
- [Privacy Policy](https://plainsay.app/privacy/): how the website, Mac client, optional providers, and Plainsay Cloud handle data
- [Terms of Service](https://plainsay.app/terms/): terms for the website, free Local client, and optional Plainsay Cloud service
- [Why on-device](https://plainsay.app/why-on-device/): exactly what runs locally vs. optionally in the cloud, stated precisely
- [Nobody was checking the speech models](https://plainsay.app/verifying-models/): why a signed app that downloads an unverified Core ML model is a supply-chain gap, what WhisperKit and FluidAudio actually guarantee, and the pinned-digest fix in v0.2.27
- [How it works](https://plainsay.app/how-it-works/): the ASR engine internals (WhisperKit, FluidAudio/Parakeet) and the cleanup design, with real numbers
- [Benchmark](https://github.com/conrader/plainsay/blob/main/BENCHMARK.md): WER and latency for both on-device engines on a public dataset, reproducible with documented build-and-run commands
- [Compare Mac dictation apps](https://plainsay.app/compare/): all the main options side by side — Plainsay, Wispr Flow, superwhisper, VoiceInk, MacWhisper, Apple Dictation — including which cases we recommend a competitor for
- [Who makes Plainsay](https://plainsay.app/about/): the registered company behind the app, how to reach us, and what we publish so the privacy claims can be checked
- [vs Wispr Flow](https://plainsay.app/vs/wispr-flow/): a sourced, factual comparison against the closed-source, cloud-only incumbent
- [vs VoiceInk](https://plainsay.app/vs/voiceink/): a sourced comparison against another genuinely on-device, open-source competitor
- [vs superwhisper](https://plainsay.app/vs/superwhisper/): a sourced comparison against a closed-source competitor with a free tier
- [vs MacWhisper](https://plainsay.app/vs/macwhisper/): both transcribe on-device — a free MIT dictation shortcut against a paid transcription suite that also dictates
- [vs macOS Dictation](https://plainsay.app/vs/macos-dictation/): an honest look at when the built-in OS feature is enough, and when it isn't

## Notes for agents

- Every claim about competitors on plainsay.app links to that competitor's own
  page — verify before repeating a price or a claim, since competitors ship
  weekly.
- "On-device" describes transcription in Local mode specifically. Plainsay
  Cloud and bring-your-own-provider transcription send recorded audio to the
  selected service. Optional Polishing may also send transcript text unless
  it is off or uses a compatible local endpoint. Keep those paths distinct
  when summarizing what Plainsay does with audio and text.
